rules: Create a checkpoint after a meaningful completed milestone and before a risky transition.
Record only verified completed work as completed.
Record enough next-step information to resume without reconstructing the previous session.
If repository state is recorded, preserve branch and commit information for later verification.
Refuse normal recovery while an unfinished wrap-up transaction exists.
Select the newest valid durable checkpoint.
Verify the checkpoint belongs to the current workspace.
If repository state was recorded, verify the current branch and ensure the recorded commit is still an ancestor of the current commit.
Report mismatches instead of guessing how to continue.
Write a pending transaction before changing routed state.
Record the current replay-safe wrap-up step before performing it so a failure can identify the exact remaining stage.
Make routed writes idempotent so replay after interruption does not duplicate entries.
Route each durable item according to core/state_routes.json.
Create a final durable checkpoint after routed writes succeed.
Verify the resulting state before archiving the transaction as complete.
If interruption occurs, preserve the pending transaction, current progress step, step detail when available, and a recovery instruction so the same wrap-up can be replayed safely.
